teachers.title: AI lesson plan generator for teachers: free options, steps and limits
teachers.h1: AI lesson plan generators for teachers, with free plans and real limits
teachers.description: How teachers use an AI lesson plan generator: MagicSchool and Khanmigo steps from their own docs, what the free plans include, USD prices from vendor pages, and where it breaks.

problem.text: Teachers lose evenings to lesson planning, grading and individual feedback. A district case study describes teachers as overwhelmed by exactly this work.
problem.quote: Before implementing MagicSchool, Twin Rivers teachers were overwhelmed by lesson planning, grading, and providing individualized feedback

teachers.lead: This is how teachers do it with MagicSchool and Khanmigo, based on MagicSchool's own docs, MagicSchool's published case study and a third-party pilot report from Michigan Virtual. Prices come from each vendor's pricing page.
goodFit: You plan lessons every week and want a structured first draft to edit, not a finished plan.
You teach to named standards and can type or pick them in the tool.
You want to start on a free plan before your school decides on a licence.
skipIf: You need plans tied to a detailed school scheme of work that you can't describe in a prompt (our view).
Your school does not allow staff to use AI tools that are not on its approved list (our view).
You teach mostly maths notation and want the tool to read typed equations reliably (see the limits below).

steps.action: Open the Lesson Plan Generator in MagicSchool and start from one learning objective.

source.text: An AI lesson plan generator turns a learning objective into a structured lesson plan.
source.quote: An AI lesson plan generator helps teachers turn a learning objective into a structured lesson plan.

steps.action: Add your subject, grade level, standards and the time you have for the lesson.

source.text: Inputs are subject, grade level, standards and available time.
source.quote: Add details such as your subject, grade level, standards, and available time

steps.action: Select or type the standards you are teaching so they are built into the objectives, activities and assessment.

source.text: Standards feed objectives, activities and assessment.
source.quote: Select or enter the standards you’re teaching to build them into the learning objectives, activities, and assessment.

steps.action: Add differentiation needs, then make versions for other reading levels or needs while keeping the core objective.

source.text: One core lesson can be adapted for different levels.
source.quote: Start with one core lesson, then adapt it for different grade levels, reading levels, or student needs.

steps.action: Review and refine the draft so it fits your classroom before you teach it.

source.quote: You can also add time constraints and differentiation needs, then review and refine the plan to fit your classroom.

steps.action: Use Khanmigo to brainstorm questions, write a lesson hook and suggest student activities for the plan.

source.text: Teachers in the pilot used it for questions, hooks and activities.
source.quote: Khanmigo proved especially valuable for brainstorming questions, writing lesson hooks, reviewing content, and suggesting student activities.

limits.text: On MagicSchool, unlimited generations, unlimited output history and unlimited AI-output editing are listed under Plus, as extras over the Free plan.
limits.quote: Every FREE feature, plus: Unlimited generations Unlimited output history Unlimited AI-output editing

limits.text: In the Michigan Virtual pilot, typing equations and math prompts made Khanmigo clunky at times, and some students found the tutor too chatty.
limits.quote: Technical challenges like typing equations or interpreting math prompts made things clunky at times. Some students were frustrated with how “chatty” Khanmigo’s AI chatbot tutor was.

limits.text: The same pilot found it worked better when started at the beginning of the school year than midway through a semester.
limits.quote: Teachers noted the importance of starting the year with an AI tool like Khanmigo, rather than trying to integrate it midway through the semester.

limits.text: MagicSchool itself frames the output as a starting point that you review and adapt, not a finished plan.
limits.quote: You’ll have more time to review the plan, make it your own, and adapt it for the students in front of you.

result.label: MagicSchool's published case study (Twin Rivers USD)

claim.text: A vendor-reported result from one teacher in a district rollout.
claim.quote: One teacher shared that she created a full week of differentiated lessons in under an hour instead of several evenings.
